theory.intro: Draw the journey, put a north line wherever a bearing starts, and look for the right-angled triangle inside the diagram.
facts: For reference angles measured from north or south, the quadrant formulas are $\theta=b$, $180^{\circ}-b$, $b-180^{\circ}$ or $360^{\circ}-b$, respectively for the north-east, south-east, south-west and north-west quadrants.
A bearing found from a triangle must be turned back into a clockwise angle from north and written with three digits.
steps: Draw the journey with a north line at each point.
Mark the given distances and bearings.
Find the right-angled triangle and an angle measured from either perpendicular cardinal side; for a cardinal journey, use its direction directly.
Choose the ratio, or Pythagoras' theorem, and solve.
State the answer in the form the question asks for.

workedExamples.question_text: A bushwalker walks $5$ km from $A$ to $B$ on a bearing of $060^{\circ}\text{T}$. Find how far east $B$ is from $A$, correct to $2$ decimal places.

A vehicle travels $8$ km from $A$ to $B$ on a bearing of $155^{\circ}\text{T}$. It then travels due north until it is due east of $A$. Find the distance it travels north, correct to $2$ decimal places.
A helicopter flies $9$ km on a bearing of $150^{\circ}\text{T}$, then flies $2$ km due east. How far east of its starting point is it, correct to $1$ decimal place?

A ship sails $6$ km from $O$ to $P$ on a bearing of $040^{\circ}\text{T}$, then $8$ km from $P$ to $Q$ on a bearing of $130^{\circ}\text{T}$. Find (a) its distance from $O$ and (b) the bearing of $Q$ from $O$, to the nearest degree.

A walker travels $9$ km due north from $O$ to $P$, then $12$ km due east to a shelter $Q$. Find (a) the bearing of $Q$ from $O$ and (b) the bearing of $O$ from $Q$. Give both bearings to the nearest degree.

A helicopter flies $5$ km from town $T$ to depot $D$ on a bearing of $315^{\circ}\text{T}$. It then flies to site $C$ on a bearing of $225^{\circ}\text{T}$. The site is $13$ km from $T$. Find the bearing of $C$ from $T$, to the nearest degree.

Two ships leave harbour $H$ together. One travels at $8$ km/h on a bearing of $030^{\circ}\text{T}$ and the other at $6$ km/h on a bearing of $120^{\circ}\text{T}$. How far apart are they after $3$ hours?

foundation.question_text:
A hiker walks $10$ km on a bearing of $048^{\circ}\text{T}$.
How far east of her starting point is she, correct to $1$ decimal place?
foundation.solution_text:
The angle between the journey and north is $48^{\circ}$.
$\sin 48^{\circ}=\frac{x}{10}$
$x=10\sin 48^{\circ}$
$=7.4\text{ km}$

foundation.question_text:
A ship sails $32$ km on a bearing of $160^{\circ}\text{T}$.
How far south of port is it, correct to $1$ decimal place?
foundation.solution_text:
The angle between the journey and south is $180^{\circ}-160^{\circ}=20^{\circ}$.
$\cos 20^{\circ}=\frac{x}{32}$
$x=32\cos 20^{\circ}$
$=30.1\text{ km}$

development.question_text:
A helicopter flies $100$ km on a bearing of $150^{\circ}\text{T}$, then flies $40$ km due east.
How far east of its starting point is it, to the nearest kilometre?
development.solution_text:
The angle between the first journey and south is $180^{\circ}-150^{\circ}=30^{\circ}$.
$\sin 30^{\circ}=\frac{x}{100}$
$x=100\sin 30^{\circ}=50\text{ km}$
The total distance east is $50+40=90\text{ km}$.

development.question_text:
A tank travels $12$ km on a bearing of $060^{\circ}\text{T}$ from $A$ to $B$.
How far due south must it travel from $B$ to reach a point due east of $A$? Give the answer to the nearest metre.
development.solution_text:
The required distance is the northward distance of $B$ from $A$.
$\cos 60^{\circ}=\frac{x}{12}$
$x=12\cos 60^{\circ}$
$=6.000\text{ km}$
The tank must travel $6000\text{ m}$ due south.
